Tables ready for apa_flextable

Source: R/apa7_tbl.R
apa7_tbl.Rd

The tibbles returned by apa_parameters(), apa_performance(), and apa_performance_comparison() have class apa7_tbl. They are ordinary tibbles for post-processing with dplyr, but in knitr and Quarto documents they are rendered as an apa_flextable() automatically. In the console they print as tibbles.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'apa7_tbl'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'apa7_tbl'
knit_print(x, ...)

Arguments

x

an apa7_tbl

...

arguments passed to the next method

Value

x, invisibly, for print. A knit_asis or flextable output for knit_print.

Details

The apa7.print option controls this behavior:

  • "auto" (default): flextable in knitr/Quarto, tibble in the console.

  • "flextable": flextable everywhere.

  • "tibble": tibble everywhere.

To render with non-default settings, pass the table to apa_flextable() explicitly, which always returns a flextable.

Examples

fit <- lm(mpg ~ cyl + wt, data = mtcars)
# Prints as a tibble in the console
apa_parameters(fit)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 6
#>   Variable `*B*` `*SE*` `&beta;` `*t*(29)` `*p*`
#>   <chr>    <chr> <chr>  <chr>    <chr>     <chr>
#> 1 Constant 39.69 1.71    .00     23.14     <.001
#> 2 Cyl      −1.51 0.41   −.45     −3.64      .001
#> 3 Wt       −3.19 0.76   −.52     −4.22     <.001

# It is still a tibble, so it can be post-processed
apa_parameters(fit) |>
  dplyr::filter(Variable != "Constant") |>
  apa_flextable()
